label: Steady
description: Constant speed, as with cruise control
why: Any speed you set; a car slower than that drives at its top speed

label: City
description: Town traffic with many stops: the WLTP low and medium phases
why: Up to 60 km/h: urban driving in the EU real-driving test (RDE), whose urban part averages 15–40 km/h including stops. Towns: 50 km/h in Germany

label: Rural
description: Country roads with junctions and villages: the WLTP high phase
why: Country roads: 100 km/h outside towns in Germany, 90 km/h on Thai highways

label: Highway
description: Highway with a stop now and then: the US EPA highway cycle (HWFET)
why: Thai highways: 90 km/h, and 120 km/h on divided four-lane highways where signed

label: Motorway
description: Motorway without stops: the WLTP extra-high phase, joined where it passes 105 km/h
why: Up to 160 km/h: the motorway limit of the EU real-driving test (normally 145 km/h, 15 km/h more for a short time). Germany recommends 130 km/h. Joined at 105 km/h so that repeating the phase does not stop every 8 km (judgement)

label: Mixed
description: Town, country road and motorway as in the WLTP test, at the test's own speeds
why: A mix of roads has no single speed: the whole WLTP at its recorded speeds

label: Traffic jam
description: Stop-and-go: the WLTP low phase slowed down to the jam's average speed
why: The jam's distance and time set its average speed
